facts.claim: Kingstonia confirmed its first H2D2 case on 21 October, a traveller now in isolation; close contacts are being tested.
facts.source: herald:2026-10-21 First H2D2 case confirmed in Kingstonia

facts.claim: The IHO confirmed sustained community transmission in two more Pacific nations on 17 October and urged nearby countries to act before local outbreaks take hold.
facts.source: herald:2026-10-17 IHO reports sustained H2D2 transmission

facts.claim: The International Health Organisation recommends vaccinating before widespread community transmission begins, not after.
facts.source: setting: The H2D2 Vaccine

facts.claim: Chief Medical Officer Dr Eleanor Whitlock, who ran the COVID testing programme, advised that waiting for widespread spread could leave our small health system dangerously exposed.
facts.source: setting: The question on the ballot

facts.claim: Both public hospitals together have about 30 intensive-care beds and roughly 40 ventilators.
facts.source: setting: The health system

facts.claim: The H2D2 surge plan assumes the hospitals can absorb only about 150 extra respiratory patients before ordinary care suffers.
facts.source: setting: The health system

facts.claim: Across the region roughly one confirmed H2D2 case in twenty has needed hospital care.
facts.source: setting: About H2D2

facts.claim: Almost all regional H2D2 deaths so far have been people over 60 or with existing illness.
facts.source: setting: About H2D2

facts.claim: Kingstonia Central Hospital has 40 unfilled nursing posts, and the hospital warned on 18 October that this limits its ability to handle a surge.
facts.source: herald:2026-10-18 Kingstonia Central Hospital warns of staffing shortages

facts.claim: The wet season starts in November, when seasonal respiratory illness already adds to hospital workload.
facts.source: herald:2026-10-18 staffing shortages; herald:2026-10-17 IHO

facts.claim: During COVID more than 1,000 Kingstonians died, hospitals ran above capacity, elective surgery stopped for most of a year and field wards went into a Crown Harbour sports hall.
facts.source: setting: The COVID legacy; The health system

facts.claim: MOUK's case is that vaccinating before H2D2 arrives makes another general lockdown less likely, which is what hurt shops and tourism most last time.
facts.source: setting: The YES Campaign

facts.claim: Nobody would be physically forced to take the vaccine; the rule only concerns entry to designated public spaces.
facts.source: setting: The YES Campaign

facts.claim: The vaccine is free to the person receiving it, at hospitals, GP clinics and pop-up sites.
facts.source: setting: The H2D2 Vaccine

facts.claim: If Yes wins, the government says the rule is phased in only after every eligible Kingstonian has had a reasonable chance to be vaccinated.
facts.source: setting: What a result would mean; herald:2026-10-20 Hawthorne commits

facts.claim: Medical exemptions would be available under the rule.

facts.source: setting: Who and what the requirement would cover

facts.claim: Proof would be a paper or digital health-ministry certificate, separate from the new national ID card.
facts.source: setting: Who and what the requirement would cover

facts.source: herald:2026-10-18 Privacy concerns rise over new national ID cards

facts.claim: Foreign visitors could use recognised overseas vaccination certificates, so travel to Kingstonia stays open.
facts.source: setting: Who and what the requirement would cover; herald:2026-10-20 Tourism operators seek clarity

facts.claim: Neither campaign is proposing to close the border; arrivals are temperature-screened at the airport.

facts.claim: The H2D2 vaccine adapts an existing mRNA platform developed during COVID rather than starting from scratch.

rebuttals.no_argument: There is no outbreak in Kingstonia, so a mandate is premature.
rebuttals.line: The first case is already here, and the IHO and our CMO both say the time to act is before spread, not after.

rebuttals.no_argument: The response is disproportionate to a disease that is mostly mild.
rebuttals.line: With about 30 ICU beds, even a mild-for-most virus can fill them fast.
It is free, phased in only after everyone has had a chance, with medical exemptions. The real two tiers are people who can wait for a hospital bed and people who can't.

rebuttals.no_argument: Medical decisions should be personal choice.
rebuttals.line: Nobody is forced to take a jab; this is about keeping shared spaces and shared hospitals working.

rebuttals.no_argument: People will be unable to work or run businesses.
rebuttals.line: Another lockdown is what closes businesses. Vaccinating first is how we avoid that.

rebuttals.no_argument: It will damage the tourism recovery.
rebuttals.line: Visitors can use overseas certificates. An outbreak is what empties resorts.

rebuttals.no_argument: It turns the national ID into a health passport.
rebuttals.line: The certificate is separate from the ID card, and the law does not allow health data on it.

rebuttals.no_argument: The vaccine is new and long-term effects are unknown.
rebuttals.line: Trials show strong protection against serious disease and no major safety concerns, and there is no-fault compensation if anything goes wrong.
The rule waits until everyone has had a fair chance to get the vaccine; what is rushed is a virus that is already at the airport.

rebuttals.no_argument: Kids will be forced or shut out of school.
The government is grabbing emergency powers.
rebuttals.line: This is a public vote the Assembly sent to the people with cross-party support. You get the final say.

rebuttals.no_argument: It sets a dangerous precedent for future emergencies.
rebuttals.line: This rule comes from one ballot question about H2D2, decided by voters, not a general emergency power.

rebuttals.no_argument: The venue list has not been published, so Yes is a blank cheque.
rebuttals.line: Nothing starts until everyone has had a fair chance to get vaccinated, the rules come from a public vote the government has promised to respect, and a No vote locks out any access rule for this whole Assembly.

rebuttals.no_argument: Vote No now and decide later if there is an outbreak.
rebuttals.line: A No vote rules out any access rule for the life of this Assembly unless there is another referendum.
The jab is free to you, and the cost of a full hospital and another lockdown is far higher.

do_not_claim: Do not claim the vaccine prevents transmission or stops spread; real-world transmission data is limited.
Do not claim how long protection lasts or that no boosters will be needed.
Do not claim the designated venue list has been published; the government says it comes after the vote via regulations.
Do not claim community transmission exists in Kingstonia; officials say there is no evidence of it yet.
Do not invent numbers, polls, quotes, deaths or case counts beyond this file.
Do not attack people as anti-vax; the No campaign officially supports voluntary vaccination.
